batch: OLP-0149–0158 First-order Logic syntax under the complete classical first-order profile
method: Fresh comparison of every exact frozen-English and Gujarati linguistic block, with independently worded reverse paraphrases for 61 representative substantive blocks. The review focuses on signature symbol classes and arity, inductive term and formula formation, unique readability, main operators, subformulas, formation sequences, free and bound occurrences, capture-avoiding substitution and all seven adjacent disclosed source repairs.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The chapter must define first-order terms and formulas, show their unique construction from a basic vocabulary, and then use recursion on that construction to assign meaning.
samples.assessment: The introduction preserves the progression from vocabulary through inductive syntax and unique readability to recursively defined meaning.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: First-order expressions are built from variables, constants, predicates and sometimes function symbols, together with logical operators and punctuation, to form terms and formulas.
samples.assessment: The language specification preserves the logical and non-logical symbol classes, arities, example signatures, alias conventions, defined symbols and expressive-completeness claims; OLSYN-001 repairs only malformed conditional-command nesting.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Predicates name properties or relations, constants name objects, and functions name mappings; apart from identity these signature-specific items are the language's non-logical symbols.
